meta.title: UK migration & demographics source inventory
principles: Prefer primary statistical producers (ONS, Home Office, NRS, NISRA, National Archives, Bank of England).
Secondary synthesis (Migration Observatory, Commons Library) labeled as such.
Do not invent numbers; this inventory describes sources, not estimates.
Flag contested fiscal/economic impact literature; list methods and opposing findings.
Use careful terminology for irregular entry: report what is measured (detections), not an unknown stock of people without permission.
meta.default_license_note: Most ONS/Home Office/GOV.UK official statistics are reusable under the Open Government Licence v3.0 (OGL). Always check each release page for third-party exceptions.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: No comparable ethnicity question in UK censuses before 1991 (England & Wales / Scotland). Cannot map ethnicity stocks continuously from 1940.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: 1991 Census (categories change in 2001, 2011, 2021/22 — breaks in detailed groups).

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: Voluntary religion question only from 2001 Census (E&W, Scotland, NI). 1851 religious worship census is not comparable (attendance/places of worship, not affiliation).
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: 2001 Census for affiliation; earlier decades not mappable on a consistent affiliation basis.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: No continuous official LTIM/IPS series from 1940. IPS-based estimates from ~1964 (paper) / 1975 (online); comprehensive LTIM from 1991; admin-based LTIM from ~2012 with major method change vs IPS era.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Indicative IPS timeline ~1964+ with strong caveats; comparable modern LTIM from 1991; admin-based series from YE June 2012 (provisional/revisable).

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: APS/LFS country-of-birth and nationality series start ~2000–2004. Census birthplace exists historically but geographies, classifications, and UK/overseas groupings change; wartime and Empire/Commonwealth definitions differ.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Census birthplace tables from 19th/early 20th century (Vision of Britain / census reports) for coarse UK vs overseas; modern APS stocks from 2004 (LFS back to ~2000).

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: Modern Home Office published asylum time series are strong from late 20th century onward (Control of Immigration / Immigration Statistics). Continuous digital tables denser from ~2000s; backlog/work-in-progress definitions change.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Use Control of Immigration / historical Immigration Statistics for pre-2010; current Immigration system statistics for recent decades. Do not back-cast backlog concepts into 1940–1970s.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: No honest time series of 'illegal immigration totals' for early decades. Small-boat detection series effectively from 2018; broader irregular detections published as official statistics from 2022. Undetected entries and visa overstays are not comprehensively measured.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Small boats daily/provisional from 2018; irregular/illegal entry routes chapter from Feb 2022. Never present as total irregular population.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.theme: Fertility by mother's country of birth
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: Parents' country of birth recorded at birth registration in England & Wales only from April 1969.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: 1969+ for E&W; Scotland/NI have separate vital statistics producers with their own start dates for analogous tables.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: Detailed cross-tabs are census-decade products or recent survey/admin research outputs; not available annually for 1940–1990 at LA level.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Census decades (birthplace historically; nationality/passports more recent); APS for national/regional stocks post-2004.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: No primary statistical series; only model-based contested estimates (static vs dynamic; average vs marginal; which public goods allocated). Cannot map a single 'fiscal impact' line from 1940.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Cite study-by-study (Dustmann–Frattini period studies; OBR FRS/EFO scenarios; MAC 2025 lifetime models) with explicit assumptions — never as fact layers without caveats.

cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.gap: 1941 Census cancelled. 1939 National Register is civilian snapshot. Mid-year estimates for 1940–47 switch between civilian / home / including forces abroad definitions.
cannot_honestly_map_early_decades.earliest_usable: Use ONS/Registrar General historical series with explicit wartime definition flags; do not treat as continuous usual-residence MYE.

sources.name: ONS Long-Term International Migration (admin-based LTIM)
sources.latest_status_as_of: 2026-05 (docs revised May 2026; series to YE Dec 2025 provisional)
sources.update_frequency: Twice yearly (end May and end November)
sources.api_csv: ONS website downloads (Excel/CSV via release pages); no single stable public REST API for full LTIM. Prefer release datasets.
known_breaks: Pre-2020 IPS-based LTIM vs post-pandemic admin-based methods (HOBI, RAPID, etc.) — not a continuous identical series.
EU+/non-EU+/British nationality groupings use different admin sources and methods; EUSS cumulative-stay methods evolving (Nov 2025 updates).
Latest ~4 data points provisional and revised when more travel history available; British nationals involve 3- or 9-month forecasting.
sources.confidence_notes: Official statistics in development (not yet accredited). Best current UK net migration flow measure for ~2012–present. Do not splice naively onto IPS LTIM 1991–2010s without a break marker.

sources.name: ONS IPS / historical LTIM timeline (pre-admin era)
sources.latest_status_as_of: Historical ad hoc / archived LTIM QMI (IPS era)
sources.api_csv: XLS ad hoc download for 1964–2015 citizenship timeline; IPS 3-series tables historically from 1975 online.
known_breaks: Estimates before 1991 use different methodology than LTIM 1991+.
IPS measures intentions (pre-admin) vs admin measures observed behaviour.
COVID IPS suspension broke continuity and accelerated admin transformation.
sources.confidence_notes: Use for long-run charts with clear discontinuity annotations at 1991 and ~2012/2020 method shifts. Online IPS from 1975; 1964–74 mainly paper/archival.

sources.name: ONS mid-year population estimates (MYE) & time series
sources.producer: Office for National Statistics (with NRS, NISRA for UK compilation)
sources.coverage_note_from_1940: Long back series exist (UK/GB/E&W). Wartime 1940–47 definitions vary (civilian vs home vs including forces abroad). 1941 Census cancelled; 1939 Register is separate civilian snapshot.
sources.api_csv: Nomis query/download (CSV/Excel); ONS time series CSV/XLSX; components of change tables include net international migration (method-dependent).
known_breaks: Census rebases (e.g. 2021/2022) revise intercensal years.
Wartime population definition breaks 1939–1948.
LA boundary changes over time; Nomis modern LA series commonly from 1991.
sources.confidence_notes: Core stock layer for the app. International migration component of change should be labeled with the migration method era. Mid-2025 UK total reported as provisional/rounded in recent releases.

sources.name: ONS Population of the UK by country of birth and nationality (APS/LFS)
sources.coverage_note: LFS-based ~2000–2003; APS-based 2004 to YE June 2021 in main bulletin series; later ad hoc/grouped estimates may appear — check latest release notes. Household survey: excludes most communal establishments.
sources.update_frequency: Historically quarterly then annual; main series paused/changed after YE June 2021 quality issues
sources.api_csv: ONS datasets accompanying bulletins (Excel/CSV).
known_breaks: COVID interviewing mode change biased non-UK-born/non-British representation; reweighting/RTI adjustments applied.
APS totals ≠ MYE totals (household vs whole population).
Main publication series ends YE June 2021; treat post-2021 stock estimates cautiously unless from a documented successor product.
sources.confidence_notes: Primary modern stock source for UK/non-UK born and British/non-British — with survey uncertainty and coverage limits. Prefer Census for detailed LA stocks in census years.

geography: down to Output Area / LA / region

sources.coverage_note: Modern quarterly Immigation system statistics; historical Control of Immigration / Asylum Statistics / Immigration statistics historical data for earlier years. Continuous digital detail denser from 2000s. Backlog/WIP definitions change; people vs cases focus has shifted in recent chapters.

sources.api_csv: ODS/Excel detailed datasets (Asy_D01 claims, Asy_D02 decisions, Asy_D03 awaiting decision, etc.). Migration transparency data for operational WIP tables (e.g. ASY_03).

Initial decision grant rates exclude withdrawals/admin outcomes depending on table.
Total asylum 'work in progress' (appeals/removals) publication lag/gaps (e.g. latest full WIP noted to June 2024 in mid-2020s chapters).
Policy regime changes (e.g. Illegal Migration Act effects on decision pausing) affect stocks.
sources.confidence_notes: Authoritative for asylum system throughput. Always label people vs cases. Commons Library SN01403 is useful secondary synthesis.

sources.license: Check Migration Observatory site terms; usually free to read/cite with attribution

sources.name: OBR Fiscal risks and sustainability / EFO — migration scenarios
sources.coverage_note: Long-term fiscal projections with net migration variants; age-profile tax/spend arithmetic. Not a micro estimate of 'immigrants' fiscal balance by visa. Assumptions change with ONS population projections (e.g. 2024 FRS vs 2025/2026 FRS migration settles).
sources.api_csv: OBR chart data / supplementary tables on release pages when provided.
known_breaks: Central net migration assumption jumps with ONS projections (e.g. ~129k vs ~315k vs ~230k long-run settles across FRS vintages).
Often assumes migrants have similar age-specific fiscal profiles to residents unless scenario varies earnings/length of stay.
Does not fully cost asylum backlog/system operational spikes in all vintages.
sources.confidence_notes: Contested interpretation: higher net migration usually improves modelled debt path via working-age inflows but does not 'solve' ageing; long-run debt still rises under many baselines. Present as model scenarios.
sources.methods: Age-specific tax and spend profiles applied to ONS population projections; sensitivity on earnings and length of stay in some FRS editions.
sources.opposing_findings: Results sensitive to migrant earnings mix, dependants, return migration, and public-goods allocation; zero/low migration worsens long-run debt arithmetic but is not a welfare analysis.

sources.name: Migration Advisory Committee — Fiscal impact of immigration (2025)
sources.producer: Migration Advisory Committee / Home Office publication
sources.coverage_note: Static (arrival year) and dynamic (lifetime NPV) estimates for specific visa cohorts (e.g. Skilled Worker 2022/23; Partner route in Annual Report 2025).
sources.api_csv: ODS data tables published alongside report (Mar 2026 update noted on GOV.UK).
known_breaks: Cohort- and route-specific; not whole migrant stock; discount rate and lifetime assumptions drive NPV.
sources.confidence_notes: Shows large positive lifetime NPV for some skilled main applicants and negative for some dependants/partner routes — illustrates heterogeneity. Contested if used as a single headline for 'immigration'.
sources.methods: In-house static + dynamic lifetime fiscal model; earnings, employment conditions of visa, public service use, discounting (~3%).
sources.opposing_findings: Lifetime estimates (Dustmann–Frattini) and OBR age-profile approaches can differ in sign/magnitude depending on group, period, and cost allocation.

sources.name: Dustmann & Frattini (2014) — The Fiscal Effects of Immigration to the UK
sources.coverage_note: Static period analysis ~1995–2011/12; EEA vs non-EEA distinctions influential in debate.
sources.license: Journal / author copyright — cite, do not republish full text
sources.api_csv: None for app ingestion; cite findings qualitatively or with permissioned extracts.
known_breaks: Static framework; period-specific; subsequent demographic/policy change.
sources.confidence_notes: Foundational reference often contrasted with later dynamic/lifetime models. Present as one study, not official statistics.
measures: net fiscal contribution by immigrant groups over study window
sources.methods: Static accounting of revenues and expenditures attributable to immigrants vs natives over years.
sources.opposing_findings: Critics dispute public-goods allocation, household composition, and extrapolation beyond study window; later MAC/OBR work uses different frames.

sources.name: Migration Observatory — The fiscal impact of immigration in the UK (briefing)
sources.api_csv: None
known_breaks: Synthesis of OBR/MAC/academic literature.
sources.confidence_notes: Best secondary explainer that there is no single correct estimate; maps assumption space for the app's methodology notes.
sources.methods: Evidence review of static vs dynamic; average vs marginal; skill/visa heterogeneity.
sources.opposing_findings: Explicitly documents conflicting study results and assumption dependence.

sources.confidence_notes: Core labour-market context by UK/non-UK birth and nationality. Pair with caveats on LFS quality.

sources_flat.name: OBR Fiscal risks and sustainability / EFO — migration scenarios
sources_flat.coverage_note: Long-term fiscal projections with net migration variants; age-profile tax/spend arithmetic. Not a micro estimate of 'immigrants' fiscal balance by visa. Assumptions change with ONS population projections (e.g. 2024 FRS vs 2025/2026 FRS migration settles).
sources_flat.api_csv: OBR chart data / supplementary tables on release pages when provided.
known_breaks: Central net migration assumption jumps with ONS projections (e.g. ~129k vs ~315k vs ~230k long-run settles across FRS vintages).
Often assumes migrants have similar age-specific fiscal profiles to residents unless scenario varies earnings/length of stay.
Does not fully cost asylum backlog/system operational spikes in all vintages.
sources_flat.confidence_notes: Contested interpretation: higher net migration usually improves modelled debt path via working-age inflows but does not 'solve' ageing; long-run debt still rises under many baselines. Present as model scenarios.
sources_flat.methods: Age-specific tax and spend profiles applied to ONS population projections; sensitivity on earnings and length of stay in some FRS editions.
sources_flat.opposing_findings: Results sensitive to migrant earnings mix, dependants, return migration, and public-goods allocation; zero/low migration worsens long-run debt arithmetic but is not a welfare analysis.

sources_flat.name: Migration Advisory Committee — Fiscal impact of immigration (2025)
sources_flat.producer: Migration Advisory Committee / Home Office publication
sources_flat.coverage_note: Static (arrival year) and dynamic (lifetime NPV) estimates for specific visa cohorts (e.g. Skilled Worker 2022/23; Partner route in Annual Report 2025).
sources_flat.api_csv: ODS data tables published alongside report (Mar 2026 update noted on GOV.UK).
known_breaks: Cohort- and route-specific; not whole migrant stock; discount rate and lifetime assumptions drive NPV.
sources_flat.confidence_notes: Shows large positive lifetime NPV for some skilled main applicants and negative for some dependants/partner routes — illustrates heterogeneity. Contested if used as a single headline for 'immigration'.
sources_flat.methods: In-house static + dynamic lifetime fiscal model; earnings, employment conditions of visa, public service use, discounting (~3%).
sources_flat.opposing_findings: Lifetime estimates (Dustmann–Frattini) and OBR age-profile approaches can differ in sign/magnitude depending on group, period, and cost allocation.
